content: The primary objective of the Aerosol-PFC application is to treat pulmonary diseases using aerosolized perfluorocarbon (PFC). This innovative technology employs an introducible jet-nebulizer (Aer-Probe, Trudell) and has been validated in multiple animal studies conducted by researchers such as Kandler and von der Hardt. The aerosolized delivery of PFC provides a safe and user-friendly method for perfluorocarbon-assisted ventilation. Patients suffering from acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) and neonatal respiratory distress syndrome have demonstrated sustained improvements in gas exchange and lung mechanics when treated with this approach. Additionally, the application of perfluorocarbon has been shown to mitigate ventilator-associated lung injury by reducing the inflammatory processes that contribute to chronic lung disease. This technology is specifically designed for perfluorocarbons and is relatively independent of their molecular structure. It offers the potential to identify and register suitable PFCs for use as respiratory drugs. Recent investigations have revealed that, in neonatal piglets with surfactant depletion-induced lung injury caused by repeated saline lung lavage, the use of aerosolized perfluorocarbon as part of a novel ventilatory strategy significantly reduced the initial pulmonary inflammatory response and improved gas exchange. In these surfactant-depleted neonatal piglets with severe respiratory distress syndrome, the expression of inflammatory cytokines such as IL-1ß, IL-6, IL-8, and TGF-ß1 in pulmonary tissue was markedly lower in those treated with aerosolized perfluorocarbon compared to the control group ventilated with intermittent mandatory ventilation. This finding was reported by von der Hardt and Kandler. Furthermore, in this surfactant-depleted piglet model, the mRNA expression of inflammation-mediated adhesion molecules, including E-Selectin, P-Selectin, and ICAM-1, was effectively reduced by aerosolized perfluorocarbon treatment, as demonstrated by Schoof and von der Hardt. Relative neutrophil infiltration in lung tissue was also significantly diminished following treatment with aerosolized perfluorocarbon. Proinflammatory cytokines and intercellular adhesion molecules involved in the acute pulmonary inflammatory response in porcine lung tissue were identified and could be modulated by this novel protective respiratory support strategy using aerosolized perfluorocarbon.
